comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Morgan Stanley report an Allowance for Credit Losses (ACL) specifically for Held-to-Maturity (HTM) securities. Citigroup's ACL for HTM securities was $137 million as of December 31, 2024, which is significantly higher than Morgan Stanley's $52 million for the same date. Both disclosures address the same financial measure and asset class, though the magnitude of credit risk provision differs substantially.

sentences.text: The HTM securities net carrying amounts at December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023 reflect an ACL of $52 million and $44 million, respectively, predominantly related to Non-agency CMBS.

comparisons.peer_topic: Allowance for Credit Losses on Investment Securities Balances
comparisons.peer_summary: The allowance for credit losses on investment securities was $152 million, $128 million, and $96 million as of December 31, 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively. This amount included a cumulative-effect adjustment to retained earnings related to the transfer of held-to-maturity (HTM) securities to available-for-sale (AFS) for the year ended December 31, 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan Chase and Morgan Stanley disclose the allowance for credit losses on investment securities. JPMorgan reports an ACL of $152 million for investment securities (including HTM) as of December 31, 2024, while Morgan Stanley reports $52 million specifically for HTM securities. Both firms recognize credit loss allowances on their secured debt portfolios, with JPMorgan's figure being notably larger.
